stanzas.sanskrit:
सम्प्राप्तो मथुरां दिनार्धविगमे तत्रान्तरस्मिन् वस-
-न्नारामे विहिताशनः सखिजनैर्यातः पुरीमीक्षितुम् ।
प्रापो राजपथं चिरश्रुतिधृतव्यालोककौतूहल-
-स्त्रीपुंसोद्यदगण्यपुण्यनिगलैराकृष्यमाणो नु किम् ॥ ७४-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna reached Mathura by noon. HE reached the garden in the outskirts and took lunch along with HIS friends. Men and women who had heard of HIS mighty actions were waiting eagerly to see his swaroopam.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
samprāpto mathurāṃ dinārdhavigame tatrāntarasmin vasa-
-nnārāme vihitāśanaḥ sakhijanairyātaḥ purīmīkṣitum |
prāpo rājapathaṃ ciraśrutidhṛtavyālokakautūhala-
-strīpuṃsodyadagaṇyapuṇyanigalairākṛṣyamāṇo nu kim || 74-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
त्वत्पादद्युतिवत्सरागसुभगास्त्वन्मूर्तिवद्योषितः
सम्प्राप्ता विलसत्पयोधररुचो लोला भवद्दृष्टिवत् ।
हारिण्यस्त्वदुरः स्थलीवदयि ते मन्दस्मितप्रौढिव-
-न्नैर्मल्योल्लसिताः कचौघरुचिवद्राजत्कलापाश्रिताः ॥ ७४-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Women in Mathura gathered around HIM. They were similar to Krishna in every respect.
They were affectionate and glorious similar to HIS radiating red lotus feet.
They had chest similar to Krishna's lustre of rain bearing clouds.
They were running all around to catch glimpse of Krishna similar to the movement of HIS eyes.
The women were decked with beautiful flowers similar to the necklaces of Krishna.
The women glowed with purity similar to Krishna's pure and majestic
stanzas.commentary_note: Facebook caption truncated at "See more"; the remaining words are not available in the intake.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tvatpādadyutivatsarāgasubhagāstvanmūrtivadyoṣitaḥ
samprāptā vilasatpayodhararuco lolā bhavaddṛṣṭivat |
hāriṇyastvaduraḥ sthalīvadayi te mandasmitaprauḍhiva-
-nnairmalyollasitāḥ kacaugharucivadrājatkalāpāśritāḥ || 74-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तासामाकलयन्नपाङ्गवलनैर्मोदं प्रहर्षाद्भुत-
-व्यालोलेषु जनेषु तत्र रजकं कञ्चित्पटीं प्रार्थयन् ।
कस्ते दास्यति राजकीयवसनं याहीति तेनोदितः
सद्यस्तस्य करेण शीर्षमहृथाः सोऽप्याप पुण्यां गतिम् ॥ ७४-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna walked around the city viewing these beautiful women making them happy. People gathered in large numbers in joy to have Krishna's darshan. At that time, Krishna saw a washer man and asked him if he can lend HIM a dress. The washer man arrogantly replied that it belongs to King and asked Krishna to go away. Krishna cut off his head instantly with HIS hand and due to Krishna's touch, washer man attained salvation immediately.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tāsāmākalayannapāṅgavalanairmodaṃ praharṣādbhuta-
-vyāloleṣu janeṣu tatra rajakaṃ kañcitpaṭīṃ prārthayan |
kaste dāsyati rājakīyavasanaṃ yāhīti tenoditaḥ
sadyastasya kareṇa śīrṣamahṛthāḥ so’pyāpa puṇyāṃ gatim || 74-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
भूयो वायकमेकमायतमतिं तोषेण वेषोचितं
दाश्वांसं स्वपदं निनेथ सुकृतं को वेद जीवात्मनाम् ।
मालाभिः स्तबकैः स्तवैरपि पुनर्मालाकृता मानितो
भक्तिं तेन वृतां दिदेशिथ परां लक्ष्मीं च लक्ष्मीपते ॥ ७४-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Another washer man gave Krishna suitable dress to wear and he was granted Vaikuntam immediately for his good deed. A garland maker adorned Krishna with beautiful garlands and sang HIS praise. Krishna wanted to give a boon to him but he only requested the boon of always being devoted to Krishna. With his answer, Krishna was pleased and blessed him with more devotion and wealth.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhūyo vāyakamekamāyatamatiṃ toṣeṇa veṣocitaṃ
dāśvāṃsaṃ svapadaṃ ninetha sukṛtaṃ ko veda jīvātmanām |
mālābhiḥ stabakaiḥ stavairapi punarmālākṛtā mānito
bhaktiṃ tena vṛtāṃ dideśitha parāṃ lakṣmīṃ ca lakṣmīpate || 74-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
कुब्जामब्जविलोचनां पथि पुनर्दृष्ट्वाङ्गरागे तया
दत्ते साधु किलाङ्गरागमददास्तस्या महान्तं हृदि ।
चित्तस्थामृजुतामथ प्रथयितुं गात्रेऽपि तस्याः स्फुटं
गृह्णन् मञ्जुकरेण तामुदनयस्तावज्जगत्सुन्दरीम् ॥ ७४-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna next met a hunch back woman who welcomed HIM and smeared sandal paste on HIM and HIS friends. Krishna made her love for HIM intense and inorder to make her outer physique reflect her inner purity, Krishna held her chin and with a gentle pull made her erect as a normal person transforming her to a beautiful woman in the world.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
kubjāmabjavilocanāṃ pathi punardṛṣṭvāṅgarāge tayā
datte sādhu kilāṅgarāgamadadāstasyā mahāntaṃ hṛdi |
cittasthāmṛjutāmatha prathayituṃ gātre’pi tasyāḥ sphuṭaṃ
gṛhṇan mañjukareṇa tāmudanayastāvajjagatsundarīm || 74-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तावन्निश्चितवैभवास्तव विभो नात्यन्तपापा जना
यत्किञ्चिद्ददते स्म शक्त्यनुगुणं ताम्बूलमाल्यादिकम् ।
गृह्णानः कुसुमादि किञ्चन तदा मार्गे निबद्धाञ्जलि-
-र्नातिष्ठं बत हा यतोऽद्य विपुलामार्तिं व्रजामि प्रभो ॥ ७४-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The people of Mathura who were devoid of sin, were offering betel leaves, flowers whatever they could and offered their salutations to Krishna. Bhattathiri exclaimed at this point that if he had stood there in Mathura with joined palms in salutation when Krishna was entering and offered HIM what he could just like the fortunate people of Mathura, perhaps he would not be born and suffering from ailments and sorrow this day.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tāvanniścitavaibhavāstava vibho nātyantapāpā janā
yatkiñciddadate sma śaktyanuguṇaṃ tāmbūlamālyādikam |
gṛhṇānaḥ kusumādi kiñcana tadā mārge nibaddhāñjali-
-rnātiṣṭhaṃ bata hā yato’dya vipulāmārtiṃ vrajāmi prabho || 74-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
एष्यामीति विमुक्तयापि भगवन्नालेपदात्र्या तया
दूरात्कातरया निरीक्षितगतिस्त्वं प्राविशो गोपुरम् ।
अघोषानुमितत्वदागममहाहर्षोल्ललद्देवकी-
-वक्षोजप्रगलत्पयोरसमिषात् त्वत्कीर्तिरन्तर्गता ॥ ७४-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna told the lady who offered sandal paste, that HE will come to her house soon and proceeded to the gate of the Mathura fort. She was gazing at the direction Krishna went. From the joy and happiness of the people, Devaki inferred that Krishna has arrived and became immensely happy. Milk started to flow from her breasts similar to how Krishna's fame reached Mathura even before HE did.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
eṣyāmīti vimuktayāpi bhagavannālepadātryā tayā
dūrātkātarayā nirīkṣitagatistvaṃ prāviśo gopuram |
aghoṣānumitatvadāgamamahāharṣollaladdevakī-
-vakṣojapragalatpayorasamiṣāt tvatkīrtirantargatā || 74-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
आविष्टो नगरीं महोत्सववतीं कोदण्डशालां व्रजन्
माधुर्येण नु तेजसा नु पुरुषैर्दूरेण दत्तान्तरः ।
स्रग्भिर्भूषितमर्चितं वरधनुर्मामेति वादात्पुरः
प्रागृह्णाः समरोपयः किल समाक्राक्षीरभाङ्क्षीरपि ॥ ७४-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Krishna entered the festive city and went directly to the hall of the great bow.
Seeing Krishna's radiance, might and beauty, the guards stood away. Even before the guards rushed to prevent Krishna from touching or taking the bow, which was decorated with flowers, HE had already lifted it, strung and broke it too.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
āviṣṭo nagarīṃ mahotsavavatīṃ kodaṇḍaśālāṃ vrajan
mādhuryeṇa nu tejasā nu puruṣairdūreṇa dattāntaraḥ |
sragbhirbhūṣitamarcitaṃ varadhanurmāmeti vādātpuraḥ
prāgṛhṇāḥ samaropayaḥ kila samākrākṣīrabhāṅkṣīrapi || 74-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
श्वः कंसक्षपणोत्सवस्य पुरतः प्रारम्भतूर्योपम-
-श्चापध्वंसमहाध्वनिस्तव विभो देवानरोमाञ्चयत् ।
कंसस्यापि च वेपथुस्तदुदितः कोदण्डखण्डद्वयी-
-चण्डाभ्याहतरक्षिपूरुषरवैरुत्कूलितोऽभूत्त्वया ॥ ७४-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The terrific breaking sound of the bow was like good and auspicious thing to happen the next day, the Kamsa vadham and sounded like the beat of the drum which symbolises victory. Even Kamsa trembled in fear and it was further increased by the cries of the guards who were hit by the broken bow.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
śvaḥ kaṃsakṣapaṇotsavasya purataḥ prārambhatūryopama-
-ścāpadhvaṃsamahādhvanistava vibho devānaromāñcayat |
kaṃsasyāpi ca vepathustaduditaḥ kodaṇḍakhaṇḍadvayī-
-caṇḍābhyāhatarakṣipūruṣaravairutkūlito’bhūttvayā || 74-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
शिष्टैर्दुष्टजनैश्च दृष्टमहिमा प्रीत्या च भीत्या ततः
सम्पश्यन् पुरसम्पदं प्रविचरन् सायं गतो वाटिकाम् ।
श्रीदाम्ना सह राधिकाविरहजं खेदं वदन् प्रस्वप-
-न्नानन्दन्नवतारकार्यघटनाद्वातेश संरक्ष माम् ॥ ७४-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna made the good people happy and scared the wicked ones. HE then went around the city and viewed its prosperity and returned to the garden in the evening. HE spent the evening with friend Sridhaama and was sharing his sorrow due to the separation from Radha. Later Krishna went to take rest, feeling happy that his purpose of incarnation to Earth was going to be fulfilled soon. Bhattathiri requested Bhagwan to protect him.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
śiṣṭairduṣṭajanaiśca dṛṣṭamahimā prītyā ca bhītyā tataḥ
sampaśyan purasampadaṃ pravicaran sāyaṃ gato vāṭikām |
śrīdāmnā saha rādhikāvirahajaṃ khedaṃ vadan prasvapa-
-nnānandannavatārakāryaghaṭanādvāteśa saṃrakṣa mām || 74-10 ||
